He averaged 19.5 points and 12.8 rebounds while making eight of his 20 3s across four Summer League games. It's a tiny sample, but it was a vision of the versatile player the Suns hoped they were drafting with the 10th pick in 2025. Anytime a big can flush down lob dunks or pop for a 3, they offer a team an ability to play with dramatically different lineups. So if Malauch translates that success to the season, Suns head coach Jordan Ott will gain a lot of flexibility with the lineups he chooses to use. What's concerning: Can Booker get back to superstar form? Last season, he posted his lowest effective field goal percentage since his third year. Despite his reputation as an elite shooter, he's made just 37.5% of his catch-and-shoot 3s since Chris Paul left. Booker's finishing regressed too. After shooting 63% at the rim over seven seasons, he dropped to 59% in 2024-25 and 56% in 2025-26, per Synergy Sports. Phoenix needs to find out whether this was an injury-related dip or the beginning of a decline. Booker's salary climbs from roughly $57 million this season to $69 million in 2029-30. If this is Booker's new normal, the Suns could get the supporting cast right and still be missing the superstar. — Kevin O'Connor Preseason Power Rankings: How all 30 teams stack up ahead of 2026-27 Fantasy watch The center spot is the battle: Oso Ighodaro has both starts, but Khaman Maluach is playing more minutes (21 mpg versus 16 mpg) despite coming off the bench. With Mark Williams out until at least February, I'm hedging my bets on Maluach. Miles Bridges' ankle injury is not considered serious. — Dan Titus Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season 2026-27 schedule Opening week : 10/21 at Blazers, 10/24 vs. Warriors Complete schedule Betting perspective 39.5 — win total +300 to win division +15000 to win NBA Finals Best case, worst case Best case: No. 6 seed A strong foundation was established last year, particularly on the defensive end. What if the young trio of Dunn/Fleming/Maluach each take steps within that context? Booker was quite good last year without shooting particularly well from deep; what does a bounceback year look like for him, in addition to everything he already does well? A sturdy defense, another year of winning the possession battle (crushing the offensive glass, forcing turnovers), internal development, and another All-NBA level campaign from Booker could have the Suns firmly in the playoff picture. Worst case: Just outside the Play-In This could simply be some combination of the league being more prepared for how the Suns want to guard, some scoring regression from Brooks, missing the 3-point shooting they sent out the building this summer, and other teams in the 7-11 range being more competitive. — Nekias Duncan Read the full Pacific Division preview

stories.title: Fever star Aliyah Boston undergoes right knee surgery following team's playoff loss to Aces
stories.summary: Aliyah Boston turned in fantastic numbers in 2026.
stories.detailText: By all accounts, Indiana Fever star Aliyah Boston turned in yet another fantastic season in 2026. The 24-year-old averaged a career-high 16.1 points per game and made the All-Star team for the fourth straight year. She was equally fantastic in the playoffs, averaging 19.6 points in a three-game series loss against the Las Vegas Aces. Boston apparently managed some of that excellence despite an ailing right knee. With the Fever's 2026 season over, Boston underwent surgery to repair her meniscus Wednesday, the team announced. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season The Fever did not announce a timeline for Boston's return, saying it would provide further updates "as they become available." It's unclear exactly when Boston sustained the injury, though she was forced to leave a game in late July after a hard fall. Boston clutched her right knee after the play, causing plenty of concern among Fever fans. Despite that, Boston was able to return and play in the team's next game, dropping 14 points in a win over the Portland Fire. Since being drafted No. 1 overall by the Fever in 2023, Boston has emerged as one of the best players in the WNBA. After winning the Rookie of the Year award in her first season, Boston turned in an All-Star season in her second year before getting MVP consideration in her third season. The Fever have steadily improved in each of Boston's first four seasons. After finishing with one of the worst records in the WNBA during Boston's first season, the Fever went 28-16 in 2026. As long as Boston is fully recovered by the start of next season, the Fever should have a shot at improving and contending for a championship in 2027.

But Acuff is the headliner as an electric scorer who can shake a defender with a crossover, toss up a floater over a big, or pull up from deep. What makes him so intriguing is how much control he has over all that creativity. At 6-foot-2, Acuff uses pace to manipulate defenses, and recognizes when to hunt his own shot and when to feed a teammate. He's also comfortable working without the ball, which could allow him to play off Zach LaVine or operate out of handoffs with Domantas Sabonis . Even if the Kings aren't winning many games, Acuff could become a reason to tune in. What's concerning: What happens if Acuff struggles as a rookie? He couldn't buy a shot during summer league and turned the ball over far too often. Point guards, especially smaller ones, are often slow starters in their careers. So if those problems carry into the regular season, what will Kings fans have to latch on to? Acuff deserves time to figure things out, but losing is easier to stomach when you can see the future taking shape. — Kevin O'Connor Preseason Power Rankings: How all 30 teams stack up ahead of 2026-27 Fantasy watch The Darius Acuff Jr. buzz is building. teamStories.detailText: Prior to the NFL season, I published an article on the preseason NFL power ranking for all 32 teams on Yahoo Sports. In that article, I explained how to use a ratings system to help price spreads, how to use it to action bets and what potential pitfalls in the process exist. I highly recommend reading that article to also lay the foundation for my NBA power ratings below. Instead of retooling the same concepts into NBA terms, I am going to provide my ratings and then note which teams I see as potential risers and fallers once the NBA regular season action begins. These are currently built off of using NBA regular season win totals, title odds to differentiate teams with the same win total number, current state of injury news, and the first few regular season games we have priced. I then add some manual adjustment. The only major difference to note in using these instead of NFL is the change in home-court rating from 1.5 to 3 points from a neutral site. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Here are my NBA preseason power ratings for all 30 NBA teams. Rank Team Rating 1 Oklahoma City Thunder +8.1 2 San Antonio Spurs +7.4 3 Boston Celtics +4.8 4 Detroit Pistons +3.9 5 New York Knicks +3.9 6 Houston Rockets +3.7 7 Philadelphia 76ers +2.9 8 Cleveland Cavaliers +2.8 9 Minnesota Timberwolves +2.6 10 Denver Nuggets +2.4 11 Los Angeles Lakers +2.2 12 Toronto Raptors +2.2 13 Miami Heat +2.1 14 Atlanta Hawks +1.8 15 Orlando Magic +1.7 16 Indiana Pacers +1.1 17 Phoenix Suns +0.6 18 Golden State Warriors +0.2 19 Portland Trailblazers -0.3 20 Charlotte Hornets -0.5 21 Utah Jazz -1.4 22 Dallas Mavericks -2.5 23 Washington Wizards -3.2 24 Memphis Grizzlies -3.5 25 Los Angeles Clippers -3.6 26 Chicago Bulls -4.1 27 New Orleans Pelicans -4.1 28 Brooklyn Nets -6 29 Milwaukee Bucks -6.8 30 Sacramento Kings -7.5 Three potential risers Houston Rockets The Rockets were second in overall market rating last season prior to Steven Adams getting injured and missing the rest of the season. At the time, they were the No. 1 rebounding team, and the NBA’s best in 3-point shooting team. The latter might be surprising, but these concepts relate: Forcing opposing teams to crash the glass leaves perimeter shooters wide open for second chance points in catch and shoot threes with high shot quality. Not only do they Rockets get Adams back, but also Fred VanVleet and they added Marcus Smart. They are a no-brainer over 47.5 on the win total, a sneaky division winner long shot, and might be dangerous in the playoffs if they can stay healthy. Utah Jazz The trendiest offseason pick is the Jazz to surpass 36.5 regular season wins, and I don’t disagree. This is like fantasy football preseason Parker Washington buzz, and it instantly paying off. Utah is loaded with young talent and has an elite coach in Will Hardy who can put it all together. They have been waiting to step up into real competition for a few years, focused on rebuilding (and tanking), and now they can hit the gas pedal. I wouldn’t be surprised if they are the biggest riser this year and in short order being a top-10 team that doesn’t look back. Dallas Mavericks This is the hardest team to figure out. A new head coach, Kyrie Irving coming back, Derrick Lively still hurt but getting healthier and Cooper Flagg — who might be an All-Star starter and All-NBA player, or might need another year of development. In full transparency, I took Flagg to win most improved player at 100-1 odds and the win total under 34.5, so am I flummoxed which way this goes. But Dallas the tools to quickly rise. If Flagg completely pops, if Irving and Lively are healthy and if coach Dusty May is an upgrade from Jason Kidd, I wouldn't be surprised if they are league average and locked into a play-in bid. Right now, they are marketably below average. DALLAS, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 25: Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks poses for portraits at Mavericks Media Day at American Airlines Center on September 25, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. Stacy Revere via Getty Images Three potential fallers Denver Nuggets The lifting Nikola Jokic has to do exceeds any other player in the NBA by a mile. The potential problem is if Jokic's efficiency drops like it did last season at the midway point and into the playoffs. Both Jokic’s 3-point percentage and finishing around the rim fell off, and his defense remains a problem. Aaron Gordon lost a step athletically, so did Jamal Murray and Peyton Watson is no longer on the team. Less depth and waning star power could cause a drop off. Portland Trail Blazers Last season, this team thrived by putting intense pressure on the ball, moving in transition and generating free throws. This year the league-mandated referee initiatives to call more offensive fouls on illegal screens and push offs could hurt Portland more than other teams. They also lost their coach, some of the back-of-house staff and a few players that fit very well, like Matisse Thybulle. They added Ja Morant and return Damian Lillard, who are good additions but don’t fit the way they play. I don’t view new head coach Micah Nori that highly, and he may struggle to put it all together cohesively. Brooklyn Nets There is one team actually incentivized to tank this season, and it’s the Nets. They owe the Houston Rockets their first-round pick and if it lands No. 1, they lose the right to draft No. 1 the following year even without keep the pick this year. Therefore, it might make sense to finish bottom three in the “relegation zone”, where they reduce the chance of landing the first pick. For that reason, they may play worse lineup combinations, they may trade Michael Porter Jr or Julius Randle and they may be a lone team that gets significantly worse this season (although they are saying otherwise publicly at the moment).

(Photo by Chris Gardner/ Getty Images) | Getty Images Following the 2024-25 season, the Spurs knew they needed an upgrade at back-up center. They had already traded away Zach Collins during the season, and Charles Bassey proved to be too injury prone, leaving them with just Bismack Biyombo to close the season after losing Victor Wembaynama to deep vein thrombosis. They responded with arguably the steal of the offseason by snatching a veteran with championship experience in Luke Kornet on a very friendly deal. It worked swimmingly in the 2025-26 regular season, with the defensive drop-off when Wemby left the floor or missed time with injury being much lower than before. However, Kornet struggled as the playoffs progressed and the opponents got stronger, and not having any other reliable depth at center forced more minutes from Wemby despite him showing signs of fatigue in the Finals, leading to one of many reasons why they lost that series. With that in mind, the Spurs went all in on size and defense in the draft a week later, taking a couple of beasts in the first round with Jayden Qauintance at 20th and trading for Tarris Reed, Jr. at 26th. While it will be a while — perhaps even a year — before we get see Quaintance, who is recovering from knee surgery, Reed has been one of the standouts in the preseason so far, averaging 5.5 points, 9.5 rebounds and 1 block. He especially stood out in Utah with 17 rebounds in 24 min, including doing his best Moses Malone impression with seven in a minute-and-a-half span in the 2nd quarter. Spurs rookie Tarris Reed Jr. 4 PTS, 17 REB (8 OREB), 1 AST, 4 STL, 1 BLK in 24 minutes vs. Jazz This guy is an absolute ball magnet pic.twitter.com/F8nNUwu6V2 — Role Player Performances (@BenchHighlights) October 13, 2026 Reed isn’t your average rookie. He’s 23 years old and played all four years in college, including the last two at UConn under Dan Hurley (who also helped make Stephon Castle into the defensive menace he is today). His 6’11”, 265lb frame, age and maturity makes him strongest rookie in his class and even compared some veteran NBA centers, and in the preseason, an argument can me made that he has looked better than Kornet. Rebs), 1 Assist (4 TOV), 1 Steal, 4 Blocks, 3 PF, and a +/- of -3 in 20:53 minutes played off the bench. I also posted it on YouTube: https://t.co/UWj0G3chVk pic.twitter.com/sw20yfO4GV — MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) October 15, 2026 None of this is to say Reed is ready to replace Kornet as Wemby’s back-up full time — he’s still a work in progress on offense and presents the same challenges on the floor with Wemby as French Vanilla, limiting his opportunities for extra minutes — but he certainly brings something the Spurs did not have last season: a strong, hardnosed big man who is a rebounding machine and won’t be pushed around by stronger centers. He gives Mitch Johnson the option to change things up in match-ups that are rough on Kornet, as well much more insurance should someone get hurt. Wemby and Kornet missed a combined 32 games last season, and while only two of those overlapped (one being the meaningless regular season finale) and the Spurs still faired well, it’s still a lot of games with only one or no reliable center. The Spurs usually managed those Wemby/Kornet-less minutes by going small with Carter Bryant, Harrison Barnes or Julian Champagnie playing de facto center, but even if they still want to do that some by design this season (and they might with Tobias Harris), they at least won’t be forced to with Reed now in tow. It’s always an over reaction to take the preseason too seriously, and it’s not like Reed has been facing the best the NBA has to offer so far, but his play has been a very comforting assurance that the Spurs handled their biggest weakness from last season about as well as possible. It will be interesting to see if he eventually supersedes Kornet in the rotation, or at least if Johnson shows no fear in putting the rookie out there when the situation or match-up calls for it.

teamStories.detailText: An annual survey of NBA general managers revealed Thursday that the league is bracing for a full takeover by Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs . After winning 62 games and making a surprise trip to the NBA Finals last season, the Spurs emerged as the survey's 2027 championship favorite, and Wembanyama was projected to win MVP and be selected as the league's best defensive player. In addition, the 7-foot-4 French center received 93% of the votes in response to the question: "If you were starting a franchise today and could sign any player in the NBA, who would it be?" The general managers did not view the Spurs as overwhelming title favorites. San Antonio received 50% of the votes, narrowly topping the 2025 champion Oklahoma City Thunder . The defending champion New York Knicks , who were picked to win the Eastern Conference, and the new-look Philadelphia 76ers , bolstered by LeBron James and Jaylen Brown , also received votes to win the title. Wembanyama, 22, was selected as the heavy favorite to win his first MVP award with 77% of the votes. Denver 's Nikola Jokic (10%) and Minnesota 's Anthony Edwards (7%) also earned nods. While Wembanyama was also selected as the "player who forces opposing coaches to make the most adjustments," the "best international player" and the "most versatile player," he wasn't the only Spurs star to receive recognition in the extensive survey. Dylan Harper , the 2025 No. 2 pick, was voted as the player most likely to enjoy a breakthrough season, topping Dallas Mavericks forward Cooper Flagg . Tobias Harris , a veteran forward who signed with San Antonio in free agency, was named as the offseason's "most underrated player acquisition." Finally, the Spurs' young core, which includes Wembanyama, Harper and Stephon Castle , was named as the league's most promising. The general managers deemed the 76ers as winners of the "best overall moves this offseason" for adding James and Brown, topping the Miami Heat and Charlotte Hornets . However, Miami's trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo was viewed as the "acquisition who will make the biggest impact." NBA.com has conducted a survey of the league's general managers for the past 25 seasons. This year's edition featured 48 questions regarding players, teams and recent transactions.

teamStories.detailText: It's not just you — or the team at NBC Sports making predictions on MVP and the championship race — who think this is the San Antonio Spurs year, a lot of NBA general managers do too. NBA.com and John Schuhmann released the annual GM survey on Thursday and San Antonio — as well as Victor Wembanyama — get a lot of love. There are some other interesting findings as well. Among the results. Who will win the NBA Championship? • San Antonio Spurs 50% • Oklahoma City Thunder 43% The Knicks and 76ers each got one vote each. Who will be named the 2026-27 MVP? • Victor Wembanyama 77% • Nikola Jokic 10% • Anthony Edwards 7% Who is the best defensive player in the NBA? • Victor Wembanyama 97% The one vote for someone else (Ausar Thompson) had to come from the Spurs, since they cannot vote for their own player, Which player forces opposing coaches to make the most adjustments? • Victor Wembanyama 47% • Nikola Jokic 33% • Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 7% Who will win Rookie of the Year? • Cameron Boozer 50% • Caleb Wilson 20% • AJ Dybantsa 17% • Darryn Peterson 13% It's worth noting that when asked who will be the best player from this class five years from now, Dybantsa and Wilson each tied with 33%. Who is the best coach in the NBA? • Erik Spoelstra (Miami) 43% • Mark Daigneault (Oklahoma City) 37% • Mike Brown (New York) 10% Which player is the most athletic? • Amen Thompson 63% • Anthony Edwards 20% • Ausar Thompson 10% Amen and Ausar Thompson are twins. Which player is the best leader? • Jalen Brunson 53% • Stephen Curry 20% • Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 7% Which team will be the most improved? • Indiana Pacers 43% • Washington Wizards 23% • Utah Jazz 13% Which team had the best overall offseason? • Philadelphia 76ers 73% • Miami Heat 10% It's worth noting that two GMs picked Charlotte here, supporting the decision to trade away LaMelo Ball. What player acquisition will have the biggest impact? • Giannis Antetokounmpo (Miami), 53% • Jaylen Brown (Philadelphia), 20% What is the most underrated player acquisition? • Tobias Harris (San Antonio) 20% • Mitchell Robinson (Boston) 17% • Naz Reid (Charlotte) 10% Which player would you want taking the shot with the game on the line? • Stephen Curry 50% • Jalen Brunson 17% • Tie between Luka Doncic and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander at 10% While these results are interesting, GMs are often quite wrong. For example, last season 80% predicted the Thunder would repeat as champions, the MVP was going to be Nikola Jokic (67%), the biggest impact acquisition was Kevin Durant (73%), and the most improved was going to be the Orlando Magic (47%).

teamStories.detailText: The NBA preseason is a time to welcome new faces, sort through lineup questions, hype up prospects, squabble over unresolved contract situations and panic about unfortunate injuries before the real competition begins. With Tuesday's openers fast approaching, let's bounce around the league one final time in search of key takeaways that will shape the upcoming season. Jump to a team: ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN NO | NYK | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS Atlanta Hawks The preseason revealed ... the backcourt is loaded With Trae Young 's salary no longer on the books, the Hawks have assembled a backcourt rotation stacked with creators Nickeil Alexander-Walker and CJ McCollum , stoppers Dyson Daniels and Lu Dort , shooter Corey Kispert and 2026 lottery pick Kingston Flemings . In fact, Atlanta had such a surplus that it traded two backup guards to land 3-and-D forward Dorian Finney-Smith from the Charlotte Hornets in September. Hawks coach Quin Snyder has used multiple starting lineups during the preseason, but he's best served sticking with last season's top group -- Alexander-Walker, McCollum, Daniels, Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu -- because it posted a phenomenal plus-20.3 net rating. That would move Dort to a reserve role after he spent the past six seasons as a starter for the Oklahoma City Thunder . Boston Celtics The preseason revealed ... Jayson Tatum will hit the ground running While Tatum returned from a May 2025 Achilles tear in less than 10 months, his shot looked rusty and he played below his All-NBA standard down the stretch last season. Then, his speedy comeback ended with a whimper when he sat out a Game 7 loss to the Philadelphia 76ers in the first round due to left knee discomfort. By taking those lumps last season, Tatum prepared himself for a smoother launch in 2026-27. The five-time All-Star was spectacular at times while posting 23 points in 27 minutes during his preseason debut , and his outside shot looked confident in a variety of situations. The Celtics must learn to live without Jaylen Brown and incorporate two key new pieces in forward Paul George and center Mitchell Robinson , but everything will be easier if Tatum is back to performing like an MVP candidate. Brooklyn Nets The preseason revealed ... Egor Demin is one to watch Be sure to include Demin on the list of 2025 first-round picks poised for major improvement in their second campaigns. While draft classmates in Dallas' Cooper Flagg and San Antonio's Dylan Harper are bursting with star potential, Demin's goal will be to move past a shaky rookie season and establish himself as a quality starting point guard. After being content to settle for outside shots as a rookie, the 20-year-old Russian was more forceful off the dribble at Las Vegas summer league. That shift was evident in a preseason win over the 76ers: Midway through the first quarter, Demin drove past LeBron James and finished a difficult layup over Joel Embiid . Veteran forwards Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle will handle the bulk of the scoring for Brooklyn, but Demin is arguably the Nets' most important player given his ability to shape their rebuilding effort. Charlotte Hornets The preseason revealed ... life without Kon Knueppel is no fun While Knueppel's record 3-point shooting got all the attention during his rookie season, his reliability was just as important to Charlotte's success. Knueppel averaged 18.5 points per game in 81 appearances, joining Young and Karl-Anthony Towns as the only rookies to hit those scoring and availability marks over the past decade. And despite Knueppel's youth and starter responsibilities, the 2025 No. 4 pick posted a strong plus-6.2 net rating. Unfortunately, Knueppel has been sidelined throughout the preseason with a hamstring injury and his availability for opening night remains uncertain. Knueppel is a critical player for the retooling Hornets, who pivoted by trading star guard LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves this summer. Charlotte's offense won't sing at full volume until its most prolific shooter is back to 100%. Chicago Bulls The preseason revealed ... Caleb Wilson will stop you in your tracks There's a special joy in watching Wilson explore the bounds of his developing game. Already in his first preseason, the 2026 No. 4 pick has raced out in transition for thunderous dunks, worked through traffic for turnaround midrange jumpers and created space in isolation to launch step-back 3-pointers. That range of offensive skills is rare for a 6-foot-10 rookie forward. Wilson has a path to becoming the best player in a strong class if he solidifies his outside shooting and smooths out his ballhandling and decision-making. His confidence out of the gate is a positive indicator, and he appears destined to be an impact defender given his length and leaping ability. The Bulls face no immediate pressure to win after changing their general manager and coach, so this season will be all about gawking at Wilson's latest highlights and daydreaming about his potential. Cleveland Cavaliers The preseason revealed ... Peyton Watson isn't the only notable newcomer Get this: The Cavaliers will pay their projected starters more than $179 million in 2026-27, well above this year's $165 million salary cap. Given that top-heavy spending structure, Cleveland will welcome any and all second-unit help. While Watson was the Cavaliers' biggest offseason addition and plugs in as a starting forward, Mario Hezonja also arrived this summer as a bargain signing after spending the past six seasons in Europe. The 31-year-old Hezonja, who once upon a time was a 2015 lottery pick, averaged 17.5 points per game for Real Madrid in Spain's ACB league last season. His primary task will be to use his inside-outside versatility to boost Cleveland's bench scoring, which ranked 25th in 2025-26. Dallas Mavericks The preseason revealed ... the Cooper Flagg hype train is gaining speed ESPN's Brian Windhorst ably documented Flagg's eye-opening performances during the Mavericks and Rockets' exhibitions at the NBA China Games. While it would be foolish to read too much into preseason statistics, Flagg averaged 25.8 points, 7.8 rebounds, 7.8 assists plus more than a steal and a block per 36 minutes in the two games. Only one player in NBA history has maintained those per-game averages for a full regular season: LeBron James. The No. 1 pick in the 2025 draft should factor heavily into this year's All-Star conversation, and there's a good chance Flagg will outperform his No. 23 spot in ESPN's NBA Rank if he continues to impact games on both ends like he did in Macao. Flagg's 3-point shot -- he hit under 30% as a rookie -- can still improve, but his combination of instincts, athleticism and work ethic is rare. And remember: He's still a teenager. Denver Nuggets The preseason revealed ... Nikola Jokic 's passing is getting more preposterous Jokic delivered the best highlight of the preseason when he casually flipped a no-look, behind-the-back pass from the left baseline past three Utah Jazz defenders to find Cameron Johnson for a right-corner 3. The assist was so on the money that Johnson seemingly didn't move his hands an inch to haul it in, and the crowd was already roaring before the shot went up. The play was a good reminder that the three-time MVP is entering rarified air as a passer. Jokic led the NBA in assists per game for the first time last season, and the 31-year-old ranks first among centers in career assists. Though Jokic enters the season ranking 41st on the NBA's all-time assist leaderboard, he's only about five seasons away from reaching the top 10 at his recent pace. Somehow, a Serbian center who wasn't selected until the second round of the 2014 draft has a legitimate chance of surpassing all-time great point guards such as Oscar Robertson and Magic Johnson. Detroit Pistons The preseason revealed ... cooler heads prevailed in the Jalen Duren saga While the negotiations weren't pretty and dragged past media day, Detroit avoided all the nightmare scenarios by finally inking the All-Star center to a five-year, $200 million contract extension on Oct. 1. The Pistons didn't fork over anything close to max money, they don't need to worry about Duren playing half-heartedly on a qualifying offer, and he can't walk next summer as an unrestricted free agent. Detroit's core of Cade Cunningham , Duren and Ausar Thompson is officially locked in for years to come. Duren took a major step to move past the ordeal by stating that he's a "Detroit Piston for life" during a conciliatory news conference. Now, the focus shifts back to the court, where expectations will be sky-high following the Pistons' 60-win campaign in 2025-26. Duren's role shouldn't change dramatically, though his defensive impact could come under greater scrutiny after Detroit traded backup center Isaiah Stewart to the Memphis Grizzlies in June. Golden State Warriors The preseason revealed ... Podz got paid Kristaps Porzingis ' mysterious indefinite absence , which came just months after he signed a two-year, $40 million contract, has further complicated what is shaping up to be a challenging season in the Bay Area. Warriors coach Steve Kerr is already trying to get by without injured star Jimmy Butler III , and Porzingis' availability concerns feel like a blow this roster can't sustain. In brighter news, 23-year-old guard Brandin Podziemski signed a five-year, $110 million rookie extension earlier this month. While the confident scorer is less accomplished than most of the other players from the 2023 draft who inked extensions this cycle, his signing reflects Golden State's need to prepare for the future with Stephen Curry , Butler, Draymond Green and Al Horford all approaching the twilight of their careers. Podziemski's $22 million AAV puts him in the same ballpark as fellow guards Christian Braun , Malik Monk and CJ McCollum. Within that group last season, Podziemski ranked first in win shares and second in scoring. Houston Rockets The preseason revealed ... Fred VanVleet is back with a bang The Rockets took a lot of heat when their offense fell flat in last season's playoffs due to spacing and playmaking concerns. In his preseason debut, VanVleet wasted no time reminding observers that he remains Houston's best solution. After missing last season with a knee injury, VanVleet posted 17 points and seven assists to key a convincing exhibition win over the Mavericks in his first game action in nearly 18 months. The 32-year-old point guard launched 12 3-pointers, twice as many as Houston's other starters combined. VanVleet's return should produce some trickle-down benefits: Kevin Durant and Alperen Sengun will have another trustworthy ball handler for late-clock and late-game situations, and Reed Sheppard should enjoy cleaner looks when he plays alongside the veteran floor general. Indiana Pacers The preseason revealed ... Tyrese Haliburton can still tug on the heartstrings Haliburton's Achilles tear during Game 7 of the 2025 Finals was one of the most heartbreaking and consequential in-game injuries in NBA history. The underdog Pacers were knocking on the doorstep of their first championship after a series of miraculous playoff comebacks, only for their All-Star guard to go down with an injury that also cost him the entire 2025-26 season. Fast-forward to last week: Haliburton made his preseason debut against the Minnesota Timberwolves at Iowa State, his alma mater. The former Cyclones star purchased thousands of tickets to fill the student sections and thanked the crowd before scoring seven points and dishing six assists in limited minutes. "It's been 472 days since I've played a game of basketball," he said. "I wouldn't want to do it anywhere else except my second home." The heartwarming scene in Ames was the perfect way for Haliburton to complete his grueling injury rehabilitation and get back to work. LA Clippers The preseason revealed ... Darius Garland had better have a career year The Clippers' injury news went from bad to worse when guard Max Strus suffered a right foot injury just five minutes into the first quarter of their preseason opener. Strus, who is expected to miss at least a month, joins teammates Brandon Ingram , Jordan Miller and Yanic Konan Niederhauser with long-term injuries. Meanwhile, Bradley Beal has been sidelined this preseason with right knee inflammation. To make matters worse, five of the Clippers' top six scorers from last season are no longer on the team, leaving Garland, a two-time All-Star point guard, as the last man standing. A passable offense will hinge on Garland shifting to a score-first mindset to compensate for the lack of firepower around him. While Rui Hachimura and rookie Keaton Wagler should also enjoy green lights, LA's offense will likely be a grind until Ingram returns. Los Angeles Lakers The preseason revealed ... surprisingly, title talk is in the air The Lakers are brimming with optimism after a transformative offseason, during which LeBron James departed and a new cast of role players arrived in Hollywood. Luka Doncic and coach JJ Redick have both floated championship aspirations, even though the Lakers were swept out of the conference semifinals last season and underwent an out-of-nowhere ownership change in August. Another potentially major hang-up: The Lakers entered training camp with two unclaimed spots in their starting lineup. While Doncic and guard Austin Reaves have an excellent bond , the Lakers clearly trail behind most of the leading title favorites when it comes to continuity. But from a talent and fit perspective, the Lakers can claim some resemblance to the 2023-24 Mavericks now that center Walker Kessler is in place. Doncic led that Dallas team to 50 wins and a surprise trip to the Finals. Memphis Grizzlies The preseason revealed ... Zach Edey is still a force With Ja Morant , Jaren Jackson Jr. and Desmond Bane all departing the Grizzlies in separate trades since June 2025, it's easy to forget that Memphis has welcomed back a major talent as it ramps up for a rebuilding campaign. Edey, a 7-foot-3 center who played only 11 games last season before undergoing season-ending ankle surgery, has returned to claim his starting spot. In Friday's exhibition win over the Bulls, Edey made his presence felt with 10 points and five rebounds in just 16 minutes. The 2024 lottery pick has the size and strength to control the glass and punish small-ball lineups in the paint, but Memphis must use this season to craft a sustainable role for him given his immense frame and history of lower-body injuries . Despite its roster overhaul, Memphis has assembled a solid frontcourt rotation that also includes Rookie of the Year contender Cameron Boozer and bruising backup center Isaiah Stewart. If Edey can put his injury woes behind him -- a big if -- the Grizzlies should be competing for a spot in the play-in tournament before too long. Miami Heat The preseason revealed ... Giannis Antetokounmpo made a good first impression It will take months to get used to seeing Antetokounmpo in a Heat jersey after his 13-year run with the Milwaukee Bucks , but so far No. 7 in white has looked a lot like No. 34 in green on the court. Antetokounmpo pummeled the New Orleans Pelicans in a recent exhibition, blasting through a crowded paint for punishing dunks, racing ahead in transition to aid Miami's preferred up-tempo approach and making the proper reads after drawing multiple defenders. Given how much time Antetokounmpo missed due to injuries last season and the career-altering trade that shaped his summer, the two-time MVP is off to a promising start with the Heat. Offseason concerns about Miami's 3-point shooting acumen haven't really materialized in the preseason, though it's fair to question whether the Heat have enough talent beyond Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo to keep pace with the East's best. Milwaukee Bucks The preseason revealed ... the veterans will get first dibs Many teams mix and match their starting lineups during the preseason to test various configurations or rest veterans, but new Bucks coach Taylor Jenkins has made sure his most accomplished players have been on the floor together. That makes sense: It will take time for the post-Antetokounmpo Bucks to mesh their holdover pieces with a batch of former Heat players who arrived in this summer's blockbuster. Milwaukee appears ready to enter the season with Ryan Rollins , Tyler Herro , Jaime Jaquez Jr. , Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner as its starting five, a group that will likely struggle to reach league average on offense and defense. As the season unfolds, Jenkins must decide when to prioritize the development of younger players such as Kel'el Ware and 2026 lottery picks Brayden Burries and Nate Ament . While that possible shift could be aided by unloading players at the trade deadline, the balance of present and future won't be influenced by draft positioning -- the Bucks have already traded away their 2027 first-round pick. Minnesota Timberwolves The preseason revealed ... the vibes are looser Timberwolves coach Chris Finch recently summarized his team's new identity in succinct fashion: "We've traded moodiness for giddiness." That checks out, given that Minnesota spent the summer pairing Anthony Edwards with LaMelo Ball in a charismatic Zoomer backcourt and moving on from Julius Randle and Naz Reid . Throw in forward Jonathan Kuminga , who was signed in free agency, and the Timberwolves have seemingly transformed from "Edwards and a bunch of veterans" to " Rudy Gobert and a bunch of young guys." But Finch surely understands that Minnesota faces serious competition in the West's playoff bracket. The initial giddiness that comes with any honeymoon period must eventually be complemented by resolve and maturity. The Timberwolves' offense should be more fun and less predictable with Ball in the mix, but discipline and focus in high-pressure moments loom as hurdles. New Orleans Pelicans The preseason revealed ... the prospects are taking a back seat The Pelicans' roster-building strategy has been puzzling. After winning just 26 games last season, are they trying to squeeze better results from a mediocre roster or are they ready to start building for the future? Jamahl Mosley, hired as coach in May , appears to be leaning toward competitiveness rather than development. Mosley opened the preseason with a veteran-dominated starting lineup featuring Zion Williamson , Dejounte Murray , Trey Murphy III , Herbert Jones and Yves Missi . In turn, 2025 lottery picks Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen both came off the bench. While Fears, 19, and Queen, 21, combined for 97 starts last season, both struggled to score efficiently as rookies and now must start over with their second coach in two seasons. The Pelicans are a team to watch in the run-up to the trade deadline: If the wins don't materialize in a meaningful way, the right move would be to hand over more responsibilities to the youngsters. New York Knicks The preseason revealed ... James Dolan isn't afraid to be the villain The NBA's parity era has been brutal on defending champions. Each of the past eight have lost key players, encountered untimely injuries, or simply run out of gas in attempts to defend their titles. The pace of modern basketball makes it nearly impossible for teams to hold up for 100-plus games in consecutive seasons, and the current collective bargaining agreement's onerous apron penalties are always lurking, ready to break up juggernauts. Knicks owner James Dolan has taken an unsentimental approach to those harsh realities: His desire to avoid the second apron led to backup center Mitchell Robinson's offseason departure, and the Knicks' recent statement that they have paused negotiation talks with Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart wasn't exactly welcome news. "Very disappointed to say the least," Towns said this week . If New York follows recent precedent and falters in its title defense, Dolan has set himself up to be viewed as the billionaire bogeyman who let money ruin his organization's rare moment in the sun. Oklahoma City Thunder The preseason revealed ... Aday Mara is found gold Mara struggled to make a positive impact when surrounded by fringe talent in the unstructured confines of the Las Vegas summer league, but the enormous Spanish center has hit the ground running with the loaded Thunder in the preseason. It already feels unfair that Oklahoma City landed him with the 12th pick in June's draft: During a standout exhibition against the Bucks, Mara finished lobs, tossed backdoor passes, left Kel'el Ware grasping at air with spin moves in the post and made all 10 of his field goal attempts. For fans of a certain generation who prize deft footwork from big men, Mara is a gift that will keep on giving all season. The Thunder clearly concluded they needed more interior size after their Western Conference finals loss to Victor Wembanyama 's San Antonio Spurs , and the 7-foot-2 Mara will make it easier for coach Mark Daigneault to manage the 82-game slog. There should be minutes available because starting center Isaiah Hartenstein has missed 37% of Oklahoma City's games over the past two seasons, and Mara has enough offensive skill and versatility to function alongside any of the Thunder's other big men. Orlando Magic The preseason revealed ... Tristan da Silva is launching It's always worth monitoring which role players benefit or suffer when a new coach arrives. In Orlando, da Silva has been reaping the rewards of first-time head coach Sean Sweeney's emphasis on spacing and ball movement. Though da Silva averaged a modest 3.7 3-point attempts during his first two seasons with the Magic, the 2024 first-round pick launched 10.7 treys per game in his first three preseason appearances. For context, only Stephen Curry , Luka Doncic and LaMelo Ball attempted more than 10 per game last season, and no player in Magic history has averaged more than 7.7. Empowering da Silva makes sense for Sweeney given that Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner are inconsistent outside shooters; Orlando's star forwards should theoretically become more efficient offensive weapons with more room inside the arc. Philadelphia 76ers The preseason revealed ... LeBron James ' latest superteam is pacing itself The veteran-laden 76ers haven't exactly raced out of the gate: In Philadelphia's first three exhibition games, James took a total of one shot and logged only 18 minutes while coach Nick Nurse rotated 10 players into his starting lineups. Given James' age (41) and Joel Embiid's injury history (extensive), the Sixers are obviously more focused on April, May and June than October and November. Don't be surprised if Philadelphia's slow feel-out period continues into the regular season. James has a history of rough beginnings when he changes teams: The 2010-11 Heat started 9-8, the 2014-15 Cavaliers started 5-7 and the 2018-19 Lakers started 4-6. Of course, Miami and Cleveland went on to reach the NBA Finals, so it's probably best to reserve judgment on the 76ers until at least Thanksgiving. Phoenix Suns The preseason revealed ... Khaman Maluach is coming along The Suns project as a low-ceiling team that won't generate much excitement beyond Arizona's borders: Devin Booker and Jalen Green form a fine backcourt pairing, but they don't exactly put a scare into the elite teams in the West. If Phoenix can escape the play-in tournament as it did in 2025-26, that will qualify as a successful season. The exception to its ho-hum vibe is Maluach, a 20-year-old center who barely played as a rookie last season. The 7-foot-1 Maluach was bigger, stronger and better than the Las Vegas summer league competition in July, and he built on that showing with a well-rounded performance against Victor Wembanyama's Spurs on Saturday. Maluach is more than just a dunker and a shot blocker: Against San Antonio, he fed a cutter from the high post, stepped out to hit a 3-pointer and came up with a steal while trapping outside the arc. The Suns should be able to give their 2025 lottery pick plenty of developmental minutes as they wait for starting center Mark Williams to return from September shoulder surgery. Portland Trail Blazers The preseason revealed ... Ja Morant should come off the bench Damian Lillard 's early returns represent some good news for the Blazers, who endured a brutal summer marked by stalled arena negotiations and a botched broadcasting hire. Despite sitting out last season because of an Achilles injury, the 36-year-old star has generally looked sharp and shot the ball well in exhibition action. Though Portland should still be careful with his early-season ramp-up, Lillard's readiness brings much-needed clarity to a guard-heavy roster. The best way for new coach Micah Nori to balance his lineups is to play Lillard alongside Scoot Henderson or Jrue Holiday then move Morant -- a surprising summer trade acquisition -- to the bench. Morant has been less impressive in the preseason, and Nori should not feel obligated to defer to his star power. Shifting Morant to the second unit also would benefit Deni Avdija , who should be treated as the centerpiece of this refashioned roster. Sacramento Kings The preseason revealed ... Maxime Raynaud dodged a bullet Though not exactly a household name, the 2025 second-round pick was a bright spot during the Kings' miserable 2025-26 season. Raynaud averaged 12.5 points and 7.5 rebounds to earn second-team All-Rookie honors, establishing himself as a rare hit for an organization with a checkered draft history. The Kings appear headed for another dismal season after losing their first four exhibition games, but they caught a break when Raynaud apparently avoided a serious right knee injury in a loss to the Warriors on Saturday. After exiting the court in a wheel chair, the 23-year-old French center was diagnosed with a patellar subluxation that will force him to sit out the season opener but should allow him to return relatively soon. Given Sacramento's roster is short on young talent to grow with 2026 lottery pick Darius Acuff Jr. , a more serious injury for Raynaud would have been a crushing blow. San Antonio Spurs The preseason revealed ... San Antonio is close to answering to its biggest question No team is facing a more consequential lineup decision than the Spurs, who must decide whether to make room for 2025 No. 2 pick Dylan Harper in a starting lineup that has included guards De'Aaron Fox , Stephon Castle and Devin Vassell . Though San Antonio's decision will shape its internal chemistry, the 2027 title race and Harper's ascent, the reigning Western Conference champions haven't officially tipped their hand. With Fox sitting out the Spurs' first three preseason games, the lineup debate has raged on in his absence. The Spurs don't have much on-court evidence to go on because Fox, Castle and Harper shared the court for only 25 minutes during the 2025-26 regular season. Victor Wembanyama's singular defensive presence nullifies most of the usual concerns about conceding size with a three- or four-guard lineup, but coach Mitch Johnson does still need a high-level playmaker to lead his second unit. When push comes to shove, San Antonio should bet on Harper's potential, move Vassell to the bench, start Tobias Harris at power forward and give the three-guard lineup an extended test drive. To make that plan work, Johnson must creatively stagger his rotations to ensure that either Fox or Harper is always on the court. Toronto Raptors The preseason revealed ... Kawhi Leonard is ready to turn the page Understandably, Leonard never had much to say about the NBA's yearlong investigation of the Clippers' role in salary cap circumvention. Even after the punishments were doled out and he was officially traded to the Raptors, Leonard sidestepped the issue at a September news conference by saying that he wanted to "move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor." The best way for Leonard to actually turn the page is to play at an All-NBA level and lead Toronto to meaningful playoff success. The two-time Finals MVP got off to a great start on that front during his preseason debut Tuesday, torching the undermanned Knicks for 21 points in only 17 minutes. Raptors coach Darko Rajakovic should be thrilled to finally have a certified alpha scorer; no Toronto player has averaged 25 points since Leonard departed for the Clippers in 2019. Utah Jazz The preseason revealed ... the offense should be light years better Utah has a strong case to be the NBA's most improved team from a watchability standpoint. Though that statement says something about how miserable the Jazz's defense was during their 22-win season in 2025-26, it also hints at the significant potential of this season's upgraded offense. Lauri Markkanen , Jaren Jackson Jr . and Keyonte George are all proven high-level scorers, and 2026 No. 2 pick Darryn Peterson should be at or near the top of his class in points per game. Importantly, the Jazz's whole should be greater than the sum of its parts because their most important players are all effective floor spacers and willing passers. After ranking 22nd in offensive efficiency last season, Utah could jump 10 spots if it gets a Rookie of the Year-worthy season from Peterson plus good health for Markkanen and Jackson. Washington Wizards The preseason revealed ... Trae Young 's pass-first pledge looks real When Young met with reporters in July after signing a four-year, $212 million extension, he made it clear that his primary responsibility was to keep the Wizards' many scoring options involved in the offense. Young suggested he would be taking a pass-first approach to help maximize a roster that features 10-time All-Star Anthony Davis , 2026 No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa , 2024 No. 2 pick Alex Sarr , 2025 No. 6 pick Tre Johnson and Kyshawn George , among other capable scorers. Sure enough, Young dished 23 assists and attempted only 16 shots through Washington's first three preseason games. That's quite the extreme makeover for a four-time All-Star guard who has averaged 18.3 shots during his eight-year career, but radical measures are in order after the Wizards ranked 29th in offensive efficiency and 28th in assist-to-turnover ratio last season.

teamStories.summary: NBA GMs answered 48 questions about the best teams, players and moves around the league.
teamStories.detailText: NBA general managers answered 48 questions about the upcoming season, and the general consensus is: They love everything about what Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs have going on right now and are encouraged about the team's future. The Spurs were the popular pick as 2026-27 NBA champion, garnering 50% of the responses, topping the Oklahoma City Thunder (43%) and the reigning champion New York Knicks and Philadelphia 76ers, who also received votes. They were also chosen as the team with the most promising young core (87%) and tied with the Minnesota Timberwolves as the most fun to watch (30%). Wembanyama was the overwhelming choice as this season's MVP winner (77%) as well as the player (93%) the GMs would sign first if they were starting an NBA franchise. The Spurs big man also earned 47% of the vote as the player who forces opposing coaches to make the most adjustments and was voted best international player (54%), best defensive player (97%), best interior defender (97%), most versatile player (57%) and most versatile defender (30%). Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Two categories where Wembanyama fell short were best power forward, which went to the Miami Heat's Giannis Antetokounmpo (70% to 23%), and best center, which was won by Nikola Jokić of the Denver Nuggets (63% to 37%). It wasn't all Wembanyama when it came to Spurs players receiving love. Dylan Harper, the No. 2 overall draft pick in 2025 and All-Rookie First Teamer last season, is the player most likely to have a breakout season (27%), beating out last season's Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg of the Dallas Mavericks, Collin Murray-Boyles of the Toronto Raptors, Amen Thompson of the Houston Rockets and Cason Wallace of the Thunder, who each received 7% of votes. Tobias Harris, who signed a two-year, $30.8 million deal to join the Spurs from the Detroit Pistons in July, is seen as the most underrated player acquisition (20%) of the offseason, beating out the Boston Celtics signing Mitchell Robinson (17%) from the Knicks . LeBron James and Jaylen Brown during a 76ers preseason game against the Brooklyn Nets at Barclays Center. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) Ishika Samant via Getty Images SGA best point guard, 76ers with best summer moves Reigning back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander of the Thunder was voted as the league's best point guard, earning 67% of the vote over the Knicks' Jalen Brunson (20%) and the Los Angeles Lakers' Luka Dončić (10%). Dončić did beat out Jayson Tatum (37% to 33%) as the best small forward. The 76ers' offseason additions, which included Jaylen Brown and LeBron James, helped earn them 73% of the vote as the team that made the best moves in the summer. The GMs feel, however, that the Antetokounmpo move to the Heat will make the biggest impact (53%) over that of Brown (20%) and James (13%) going to the 76ers. Other notable results: The Indiana Pacers (43%) will be the most improved team this season, the GMs believe, over the Washington Wizards (23%). Who will win Rookie of the Year? Memphis Grizzlies first-round draft pick Cameron Boozer (50%) is the most popular choice ahead of Caleb Wilson of the Chicago Bulls (20%) and No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa of the Washington Wizards (17%). But Dybantsa and Wilson win out when it comes to the future. The GMs believe both first-year players (33%) will be the best in five years. Boozer garnered 23% of support. The Heat's Erik Spoelstra is the best head coach (43%) over Oklahoma City's Mark Daigneault (37%). Spoelstra is also tied for the best manager/motivator of people (23%) with Golden State's Steve Kerr and Boston's Joe Mazzulla. As far as tacticians go, the Pacers' Rick Carlisle (30%) was the choice over Tyronn Lue of the Los Angeles Clippers. Carlisle was also voted (47%) as the coach who runs the best offense. Which current player will make the best head coach someday? Celtics guard Mike Conley got 50% of the votes over the Pacers' T.J. McConnell (13%) and Brunson (10%). Game on the line, which player are GMs choosing to take the last shot? Stephen Curry (50%), of course. Brunson did get 17% of votes. GMs were not able to vote for their own team, players or coaches. The 2026-27 NBA season tips off on Tuesday, Oct. 20, with a triple-header. The Pistons will host the Celtics at 3 p.m. ET before the Knicks raise their championship banner ahead of taking on the 76ers at 7 p.m. ET. The night will end with the Thunder visiting the Spurs at 9:30 p.m. ET.

stories.title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts ruled out vs. Panthers with blood clot in calf
stories.summary: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers due to a superficial blood clot in his calf.
stories.detailText: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers due to a superficial blood clot in his calf, the team announced Thursday. Hurts was listed as a full participant in Friday's practice before the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars with a calf injury. He had no injury designation for Sunday's game in London. The Eagles released a statement detailing the process that led to the discovery of the blood clot. "On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf," the team said. "He informed the medical staff he had been cleated during the Rams game on October 4th. This was his first treatment session for the calf injury following the game, after having practiced in full both Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, Jalen received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the practice report. "Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team's flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia." The Eagles said Hurts "played without limitation" against the Jaguars before receiving treatment Monday and Tuesday then practicing in full Wednesday. "On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority," the Eagles said. The Eagles have remained in communication with the NFL office throughout the process, the team said. Asked about the injury Wednesday, Hurts indicated he got "nicked" against the Rams while hinting that the lead-up to the Jaguars game was not ordinary. "It was a very unique experience, to say the least. I don't want to get into the details of kind of leading up to the game and whatnot, but got nicked up in the Rams game," he said. Hurts did not take the field until right before the opening kickoff against Jacksonville and rode the stationary bike between series. He indicated both actions were related to the calf. He completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and one touchdown in the 19-17 loss to the Jaguars. Hurts, 28, has 933 passing yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions this season. Tanner McKee is expected to start in place of Hurts against the Panthers. Carolina linebacker Jaelan Phillips , who played against McKee in practice last season when McKee was a scout team quarterback with the Eagles, said the quarterback change won't impact the Panthers' preparation. "We prepare the same way," Phillips said. "It doesn't really matter who they have, we've got to execute the way we need to. Obviously, it changes what they might do, which then changes a little of what we might do. But it's not like it's a different mentality. We've got to prepare for everything the same way." ESPN's Mike Kaye contributed to this report.

stories.title: Seahawks elevate pair of newcomers from practice squad for Broncos game
stories.summary: The special teams gunner is set to make his debut with Seattle.
stories.detailText: Through the first month of the season, the Seattle Seahawks struggled with kickoff coverage and rank near the bottom of the league in yards allowed per return, but they’re set to gain a key special teams asset ahead of a crucial Week 6 road matchup against the Denver Broncos. The team announced they’ve elevated wide receiver and special teams gunner Irv Charles, as well as linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo from the practice squad. Both will make their team debuts. Acquired from the New York Jets in May , Charles missed the first five games while on injured reserve with a knee issue but was designated to return to practice on October 7. Seattle activated him to the active roster on Tuesday , although, he was released a day later to make room for running back Velus Jones Jr . As a vested veteran, Charles wasn’t subject to waivers and rerouted to the practice squad. Upon his return, Charles is expected to play a key role on kick and punt returns—areas where he’s highly regarded. On the defensive side, Ciarlo’s elevation was expected given the Seahawks will be without starting linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle) and Chazz Surratt (chest), leaving a thin group even thinner. The third year linebacker went undrafted out of Army in 2024 before signing with the Jets, but missed his entire rookie season with a knee injury. He was released in May, 2025 and spent time with the Buffalo Bills, Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans prior to signing with the Seahawks on September 30.

stories.title: Aaron Rodgers vs. Todd Bowles should be quite a chess match when Steelers visit the Buccaneers
stories.summary: — Todd Bowles will have to be quite creative to surprise Aaron Rodgers.
stories.detailText: TAMPA, Fla. -- — Todd Bowles will have to be quite creative to surprise Aaron Rodgers . Known for his complex defensive schemes and disguising his blitz packages, Bowles and his Tampa Bay Buccaneers are facing an elite quarterback who has seen everything in a distinguished NFL career. Rodgers just passed Peyton Manning to move into third place for most career passing touchdowns, including the postseason. It’ll be quite the chess match when Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2) face off against the Buccaneers (1-4) on Sunday. “Obviously, Todd has a history of bringing a lot of pressures,” Rodgers said. “We’ll be ready for those. But he brings a lot of stuff you haven’t seen before, so, good disguise team, good pressure team. We’ll have to pick them up and get the ball out.” The 42-year-old Rodgers, a four-time NFL MVP, has thrown three TD passes in three straight games. But he’s 1-2 against Bowles’ Tampa Bay defenses, including a loss in the 2020 NFC championship game. Rodgers threw for 442 yards and two touchdowns and ran for two scores against Bowles and the Jets in a 44-38 overtime victory with Green Bay in 2018. “It’s a nightmare game-planning against him,” Bowles said. “He’s difficult because he’s extremely intelligent. His football IQ is unbelievable. He’s extremely accurate with the football, and he can dissect things before the play even happens. He can see it when the huddle breaks. He can see a tip here or there that a lot of people can’t see that lets him know what it is, and he knows where to go with the football and he’s very bright that way. He can bait you into a lot of things. He has a lot of tricks to the trade he (has) learned over the years." Those tricks haven't always translated to great starts on the road in Tampa, where Rodgers is just 2/3 in his career and has two of his six career three-interception games at Raymond James Stadium. Asked if he gets nostalgic visiting certain venues for the final time as he wraps up his 22nd and final season, Rodgers just shook his head. “I haven’t really thought a whole lot about it, but there’s a few places I’m glad I don’t have to go back to, for sure,” he said with a laugh. Meanwhile, the Steelers will go against an undrafted rookie quarterback who has been impressive in two starts. Jalon Daniels led the Buccaneers to a victory at Dallas last week, playing an efficient, turnover-free game. With Baker Mayfield still recovering from a dislocated thumb, Daniels will make his third straight start. A dynamic run game took pressure off Daniels against the Cowboys. Bucky Irving ran for 165 yards and the Bucs finished with 241 on the ground. Overall, Daniels has come a long way since beating out veteran Jake Browning for the backup job in training camp. “Trusting my eyes, trusting what the defense was giving me and taking No. 1 or No. 2 in the progression, and if you see a hole, and it’s a gaping, wide-open hole, probably take it because, at the end of the day, you’re trying to move the sticks," Daniels said. Need to know Pittsburgh (3-2) at Tampa Bay (1-4). When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, CBS. Latest odds: Steelers by 2 1/2. Against the spread: Steelers 3-2; Buccaneers 1-4. Last week: Steelers beat the Colts 34-22; Buccaneers beat the Cowboys 24-16. Last meeting: Steelers beat the Buccaneers 20-18 on Oct. 12, 2022, in Pittsburgh. Series record: Steelers lead 10-2 Matchup to watch Buccaneers right tackle Luke Goedeke vs. Steelers edge rusher T.J. Watt . The four-time All-Pro Watt is an elite pass rusher who has 119 1/2 sacks. It'll be a tough challenge for Goedeke, who had multiple penalties last week. Stats and stuff — Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers is 3-4 vs. the Buccaneers, including the playoffs. — Rodgers has thrown three TD passes in three straight games, the first Steelers QB to do that since Terry Bradshaw in 1982. — The Steelers are hurting at wide receiver. Michael Pittman Jr ., Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek are out with injuries, leaving just rapidly improving rookie Germie Bernard and a cast of largely unknowns behind DK Metcalf . — Steelers RB Jaylen Warren had career-high 188 scrimmage yards last week and became the sixth player to have an 80-yard TD receiving and 50-yard TD rushing in the same game. Warren has 490 combined yards over his past three games. — The Steelers are 27-6 against rookie QBs since 2007. — Pittsburgh is 0-2 on the road this season, giving up an average of 349.5 yards in losses to New England and Cleveland. — The Buccaneers ran for 241 yards against the Cowboys, including 165 by Bucky Irving. — Buccaneers QB Jalon Daniels was 19 of 25 for 189 yards and one TD vs. Dallas. — Buccaneers RB Kenny Gainwell had a career high in scrimmage yards (1,023) with Pittsburgh last season. — WR Emeka Egbuka has 21 catches for 192 yards and one TD for the Buccaneers. — OLB David Walker has two sacks to lead the Buccaneers. — Buccaneers kicker Chase McLaughlin is 10 for 10 this season. ------ AP Sports Writer Will Graves in Pittsburgh contributed. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Glorious Seahawks vs. Broncos throwback uniform showdown is NFL's best this season
stories.summary: The Seahawks vs. Broncos "Thursday Night Football" throwback showdown leads columnist Nate Davis' list of the Top 10 NFL uniform matchups of 2026.
stories.detailText: Rest assured, when you log in for Thursday night’s game between the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos on Amazon Prime, you’re in the right place – not getting high-definition NFL Films clips of John Elway trying to beat Kenny Easley in coverage. But what could be the best game of Week 6 of the 2026 season is certainly going to have a retro vibe calling back the 1970s, ‘80s and 90s, when the Broncos and Seahawks were AFC West rivals. That’s because both clubs will be donning glorious throwback uniforms – vintage looks a good subset of both fan bases would like to see restored as these teams’ primary looks. (This is probably a good time to remind them neither team won a Super Bowl in these classic threads, but details, details.) The pleasing visual will probably serve – definitely serve in this football fashionista’s opinion – as this season’s top uniform matchup. And, lest you take issue with my Elway-Easley scene setter, yes, Denver’s throwbacks are technically a callback to the pre-Elway 1977 team , the first in Broncos history to reach the Super Bowl (they were blown out by the Dallas Cowboys in Super Bowl 12 ). Seattle’s are specifically tied to the 1990s, after the career of Easley, a Hall of Fame safety , had ended. The @Seahawks and @Broncos will both be wearing their throwback uniforms on TNF 🔥 @SEAvsDEN – Thursday 8:15pm ET on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/UkCOsxYgpq — NFL (@NFL) October 13, 2026 But, hey, 2026 basically looks like 1986 – and kudos to the NFL for allowing both teams to wear their vibrant home jerseys. Also, take heart, 12s, Seattle’s new ownership has already announced it will be bringing back throwback white roadies in 2027. The Broncos need not concern themselves there as they enter their Week 6 matchup with a 5-0 record since introducing the “Mile High Collection” throwbacks in 2024. But Broncos-Seahawks isn’t the only game worth tuning into this season purely for the football aesthetics. Here are nine other games you should take a look at – literally – this season: Oct. 25, 2026: Miami Dolphins at New York Jets Two teams likely to be drafting very early next spring will (basically) throw it back to their Super Bowl glory years – glory year in the Jets’ case. And, no, these throwbacks aren’t exacting replicas of what these teams wore in the 1960s and ‘70s, but close enough. Notably, this matchup marks the 40th anniversary of New York’s 51-45 overtime defeat of the Dolphins in the Meadowlands, one of the most exciting games in NFL history, though the Jets wore the forerunners of their current unis in that game, when Ken O’Brien outdueled Dan Marino in a game that featured nearly 1,100 yards of total offense. Nov. 8, 2026: New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles Similar to Seahawks-Broncos, these teams will meet in throwbacks from the NFL’s golden age of uniforms – the late 1970s into the 1990s – and, arguably, the golden age of the NFC East … though no one cared about the (St. Louis) Cardinals then, either, and that was long before the Eagles finally won their first Super Bowl. Regardless, few unis beat Philly in silver and Kelly Green, and the block “GIANTS” logo and road uniforms that actually have blue (imagine!) elements are also winners. Nov. 15, 2026: San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys Speaking of classic rivalries, this pairing will take you back to 1994, perhaps the peak of the rivalry between the Niners and “America’s Team.” That year was also the NFL’s 75 th anniversary, and the 49ers celebrated by wearing throwbacks from the 1950s, which had distinctive drop shadowing to the jersey numbers. Wearing those threads, San Francisco went on to win its fifth – and most recent – Super Bowl while ending the three-peat bid of the 1990s Dallas dynasty. The Cowboys will generally sport their classic home look for this game but will add a red centerline stripe to their helmets. Originally used for a red, white and blue effect during the 1976 season to celebrate America’s bicentennial, the Cowboys now wear the red stripe once annually to celebrate the league’s “Salute to Service” program, which celebrates veterans, and the club’s own celebration of Medal of Honor recipients close to Veterans Day. Nov. 16, 2026: Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens The Bolts don’t win much, especially this year, but they’re royalty when it comes to football haberdashery. And they’ll face the Ravens for this Monday night affair, one when Baltimore will debut its new "Darkness Helmet,” a matte black lid with a forward-facing black and shaded Ravens logo with red eyes. Topping the team’s new black jersey and pants, it should look especially sinister as a new component to the team’s always impressive prime-time, pre-game hype show. Nov. 25, 2026: Green Bay Packers at Los Angeles Rams The league’s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game will take you back to the 1960s … if they played games in a covered football cathedral like SoFi Stadium in the 1960s. But the Rams will debut their “Fearsome White” alternates, a new spin on the unis they wore in the 1960s and ‘70s when their “Fearsome Foursome” defensive line anchored the team. These threads feature mostly white jerseys and pants and, notably, white horns on the helmet. No yellow or gold (or “Sol”). Though the Rams occasionally used white horns after relocating to LA in 2016, they weirdly crowned their St. Louis-era uniforms. They haven’t worn anything approximating the Fearsome Whites since 1972. Dec. 6, 2026: Los Angeles Chargers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Bolts experienced a rare uniform fail when they debuted their “Charger Power” alternates last season – the first time they’d worn gold jerseys (with gold pants) … in a game they lost to the Indianapolis Colts. Meant to celebrate the “Air Coryell” teams in San Diego, the “Charger Power” unis hit the road this year – with white pants this time, which are quite an improvement – while the Bucs will wear their original “Creamsicle” road uniforms at home, a selection they had not used since 1976 before bringing them back in 2025 to celebrate the franchise’s 50 th season. Dec. 20, 2026: Detroit Lions at Minnesota Vikings The Vikes will debut their Norse-inspired “Rivalries” uniforms in this game – and they might be the best alternates ever, at least in terms of a creative, fashion-forward perspective. "(W)e had the freedom to explore different shades, tones and combinations. We could also develop entirely new number styles and wordmarks," said the team's senior creative director, Alicia Dreyer when the uniform was unveiled in August. "The added flexibility allowed us to more fully embrace the Viking identity and incorporate elements we had not previously been able to explore." Also, per the Vikings, the "design was inspired by the textures of Viking armor; natural materials such as iron, wood and stone that connect both Minnesota and the ancient Viking world; and elements from Minnesota Vikings game-day rituals, including runestones, the Gjallarhorn and the Skol Drum." Can’t wait to see them under the “Sunday Night Football” lights. Dec. 25, 2026: Los Angeles Rams at Seattle Seahawks This highly anticipated Christmas matchup between the best teams from 2025 – and maybe 2026? – will also be the first game featuring both teams wearing their “Rivalries” uniforms. The Seahawks first wore their “High Decibel Zone” look – which the players love – in Week 16 last year, their memorable 38-37 overtime defeat of the Rams which helped Seattle secure the No. 1 playoff seed and helped launch their flight plan to victory in Super Bowl 60 . Jan. 3, 2027: Kansas City Chiefs at Los Angeles Chargers This currently projects as a near-meaningless Week 17 game. But looking at the Bolts is always fun, if not watching them play. They’ll don their all-navy “Super Chargers” alternates – the best of their many gorgeous looks, in my opinion, evoking memories of Junior Seau, LaDainian Tominson and, especially, the 1994 team which was the only one in club history to play in the Super Bowl – for this AFC West clash. stories.title: Colts RB Jonathan Taylor not fretting slower start than usual
stories.summary: Taylor may have lower numbers than usual, but he's still in the top 10 in rushing yards and rushing TDs.
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS -- The true indication of a player's greatness might be what kind of reaction comes when they produce average performances. Take Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor , for instance. He appeared for his scheduled media gathering with local reporters on Thursday, and the conversation quickly turned to the lack of the explosive plays for which he has become famous. "Explosive runs?" Taylor said. "You talking about the 40-, 50-yard touchdowns? "Everybody loves those." Taylor then pointed out that he registered a 20-yard run in last Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers , one of his longest of the season. A fair point, but the retort might have had more impact if Taylor hadn't had two runs of 80 yards or longer just last season. The whole exchange was a good reminder of the lofty standards Taylor is held to. It's why his current 3.9-yard-per-rush average is somewhat alarming for a player who has averaged 4.8 yards per carry in his career. It's why his third-down conversion rate of 33.3% is noticeable, considering his career mark is 47.3%. And, perhaps more than anything, it's why it's so remarkable that Taylor hasn't posted a 100-yard rushing performance in 11 months. It's all a little jarring when the subject is a player who is one of the best rushers of his generation, one coming off a 1,585-yard season in 2025, when he matched a career-high 18 rushing touchdowns. "It's still early and obviously everyone wants to come out the gate fast, similar to how we did last year," he said. "But, like I mentioned, it's a long season. It's a very long season." The Colts (2-3) have not produced the offensive fireworks they thought were possible in 2026. They drew confidence from their fast start in 2025, when quarterback Daniel Jones and the passing game took off and Taylor ran past opponents. But in the latter stages of the season, after Jones was sidelined with an Achilles tear and the Colts became easier to defend, Taylor started to see slippage in his production. That has continued this season, with Jones off to a slow start after his recovery, with deep-threat receiver Alec Pierce sidelined by a recurrence of his heel injury and the Colts experiencing overall lethargy on offense. Indianapolis ranks 22nd in expected points added, 29th in yards per play (4.6) and 25th in third-down conversions (35.3%). The lack of explosive threats has made them easier to defend, and that has allowed Taylor to become the focal point of opposing defenses. The Steelers used a five-man defensive front at times in their win over Indianapolis. The Tennessee Titans , who visit the Colts on Sunday, will undoubtedly take a similar approach and emphasize stopping Taylor in their game plan. Tennessee ranks fourth against the run, allowing 3.5 yards per rush. To be clear, Taylor has still managed to be effective in 2026. He ranks 10th in rushing yards per game (79.6), with 398 rushing yards and six touchdowns. Those inside the organization emphasize that he is getting the most out of his runs. Running backs coach DeAndre Smith on Thursday said, "When you're elite like that, those guys actually get more [yardage] than what's actually blocked. So, it's always been the standard here that he'll make spectacular plays." Currently, the types of defensive tactics the Colts are seeing don't allow as many of those. "When you don't have to blitz and you can just play four guys up front, and do a lot of damage, then that keeps seven people back," Smith said. "You're trying to maneuver through several layers of a defense." Taylor is among the league's most patient runners, able to wait for blocks to materialize and for defenders to commit to an angle before making his devastating cuts. And he'll need to continue displaying patience in the grander sense, too, as he waits for the opportunities for the big plays he believes are coming. "It's about maybe squeezing out 1 or 2 extra yards," he said. "Now maybe that's 4.1 [yards per carry], maybe that's 4.2. Maybe you have a 50-yard touchdown, now it's at 4.5." He added, of those thrilling big plays, "Those will come. It's still early."

stories.title: Packers Injury Report: Keisean Nixon returns to practice
