stories.detailText: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we wrote earlier today, the Green Bay Packers no longer have the freedom to have players on the 53-man roster miss games with injury without making some sort of corresponding moves to bring in their replacements . Here’s the good news: One player who did not practice on Wednesday, cornerback Keisean Nixon, practiced on Thursday, even though he was limited. The bad news? Receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), defensive lineman Javon Hargrave (Achilles), defensive lineman Jonathan Ford (calf) and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) missed a second straight day of practice. The assumption is that Hargrave will go on the injured reserve soon for his torn Achilles, while it appears that Moore will miss a couple of weeks with an ankle injury that has left him in a boot and on a scooter. While St-Juste’s and Ford’s injuries haven’t been discussed much in press conferences, their missing back-to-back practices means that their chances to play on Sunday are likely in doubt. At minimum, the team will need to bring up an extra receiver this week, be it Savion Williams (who is currently practicing with the team despite being on the injured reserve list) or a practice squad option (Isaiah Neyor, Quincy Skinner Jr. or Coleman Owen). Once Hargrave goes on the injured reserve, the Packers will have two open roster spots on the 53-man roster, and they’ll also have the option to use two game-day practice squad elevations this week, which should help smooth out the holes on the roster if the injured players can’t suit up against the Dallas Cowboys. To keep it simple, think of the Packers’ roster situation this way: Functionally, with the expectation that Hargrave will go on IR soon, the team has a 51-man roster. A game-day roster is made of 48 players, and the Packers rarely carry more than 8 offensive linemen into games, but they’re currently carrying 11 on the active roster. You can basically lock in that Green Bay will scratch three offensive linemen already, leaving them with the minimum of 48 players — the amount needed to fill a game-day roster…but that’s with the assumption that all of those players will be healthy. So for every injured player who can’t play on Sunday (besides offensive linemen or Hargrave), the team will need to backfill (likely at the same position). #Packers injury report: NT Jonathan Ford was a DNP, which means they may be very thin at the position Sunday vs. the #Cowboys . pic.twitter.com/UF0fNfYfNI — Tom Silverstein (@TomSilverstein) October 15, 2026 Beyond the non-participants, the following players were listed as limited for a second-straight practice: guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), defensive lineman Anthony Campbell (ankle), offensive lineman Jacob Monk (quadricep), defensive lineman Jordon Riley (Achilles, practice window player), receiver Savion Williams (ankle, practice window player) and defensive lineman Devonte Wyatt (ankle, practice window player). On the Cowboys’ end of the injury report, their non-participants on Thursday were cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring). Their limited players in practice were linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) and cornerback Ameer Speed (knee). To say the least, one of these teams is a bit more banged up than the other.

stories.title: Packers seek to build on their momentum as Cowboys attempt to bounce back from ugly loss
stories.summary: — Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers are aiming to build off their best win of the season as they prepare to host a Dallas team attempting to bounce...
stories.detailText: GREEN BAY, Wis. -- — Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers are aiming to build off their best win of the season as they prepare to host a Dallas team attempting to bounce back from an embarrassing loss. The Packers (3-2) are above .500 for the first time this season after a 31-7 blowout of the Chicago Bears . They're chasing their third straight win in a Sunday night matchup with the Cowboys, who fell 24-16 at home to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Oct. 8. “You’ve got to keep stacking,” Love said. “We talk about it in the locker room all the time and team buildings. You have a game like that, you’ve got to be able to follow it up with another great performance.” The Cowboys (2-3) are eager to make up for their bad performance against Tampa Bay and fix their slumping defense. Dallas has allowed a league-high 6.4 yards per play. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer brought longtime NFL defensive coach Mike Pettine out of retirement this week to work as a senior assistant to beleaguered defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Pettine was the Packers’ defensive coordinator from 2018-20. “We have to coach better,” Schottenheimer said. “We’ve got to play better. I think our players will be the first ones to say there’s things that they need to do better. There’s things I need to do better. And so no one is sitting here pointing the fingers at Christian Parker. But as the head coach, you have to make decisions that you think helps you win games. And that’s in all three phases.” These teams met last year at Arlington, Texas, and tied 40-40 in a shootout that ended with nine straight scoring drives. It was the most consecutive scoring drives to end a game since at least 1933. Last year’s matchup also marked the return of Micah Parsons to AT&T Stadium, a month after the Cowboys traded the superstar edge rusher to the Packers. Parsons won’t be playing Sunday as he continues his recovery from a torn ACL that ended his 2025 season, but this game features two former Packers first-round picks coming to Lambeau Field as visiting players for the first time. Defensive tackle Kenny Clark earned three Pro Bowl selections in nine seasons with the Packers before heading to Dallas in the Parsons trade. Linebacker Rashan Gary went to Dallas in a separate trade earlier this year after collecting 46 1/2 sacks for the Packers from 2019-25. “It’s going to be awesome to get to go back to Lambeau, play a game and go up there to go get a win,” Clark said. “I’m really excited.” Need to know Dallas (2-3) at Green Bay (3-2). When/where to watch: Sunday, 8:20 p.m. EDT, NBC. Latest odds: Packers by 1. Against the spread: Cowboys 3-2; Packers 2-3. Last week: Cowboys lost 24-16 at home to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers; Packers won 31-7 at home over the Chicago Bears. Last meeting: Packers and Cowboys tied 40-40 in Arlington, Texas, on Sept. 28, 2025. Series record: Packers lead 22-17-1. Matchup to watch Cowboys passing game vs. Packers pass defense: Green Bay has seven interceptions while allowing only six touchdown passes this season, but the Packers haven’t faced any quarterbacks of Dak Prescott’s caliber. Prescott has thrown for over 275 yards in each of his last four games. Dallas has one of the NFL’s top receiving duos in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens . Stats and stuff — Cowboys RB Javonte Williams has six touchdown runs to rank fourth in the league, behind Buffalo’s Josh Allen (eight), Baltimore’s Derrick Henry (seven) and Detroit’s Jahmyr Gibbs (seven). — Pickens has 1,784 yards receiving since the start of the 2025 season. The only NFL players with more during that time are Seattle’s Jaxon Smith-Njigba (2,376) and the Los Angeles Rams’ Puka Nacua (2,052). — Green Bay has won 10 of its last 12 meetings with Dallas, including regular-season and playoff matchups. Dallas’ only win during that stretch was a 30-16 victory at Lambeau Field on Oct. 16, 2016. — The Packers have won their last nine October games. — Love has thrown at least two touchdown passes in each of the Packers’ first five games. He has passed for more than 300 yards three times this season. — Christian Watson and Matthew Golden make Green Bay the only team with two players ranked among the top 10 in the NFL in yards receiving. Watson is fifth with 474 and Golden is ninth with 397. — Packers S Xavier McKinney has three interceptions to tie Minnesota’s Byron Murphy Jr . for the NFL lead. McKinney picked off two passes in the Bears game. ------ AP Pro Football Writer Schuyler Dixon in Frisco, Texas, contributed to this report. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.title: Ravens-Falcons game without Lamar Jackson averages 17 million viewers
stories.summary: Star players continue to sell.
stories.detailText: Star players continue to sell. The absence of star players continues to not. Without two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson available for Sunday night's game between the Ravens and Falcons, the NBC broadcast averaged 17 million, per Nielsen's weekly audience report. Yes, the game was up against a Brewers-Dodgers game on Fox that drew 10 million. But not having Lamar Jackson playing in the game surely made an impact. With Tyler Huntley replacing Jackson, the game itself delivered, with the Ravens winning in overtime, 30-23. The showing underscores the NFL's desire to protect franchise quarterbacks. The players who most move the needle are more likely to draw roughing-the-passer fouls than the rest. Not having the best of the best players available will indeed have a negative impact on the NFL's business interests. Ultimately, there wasn't much daylight between Ravens-Falcons and Buccaneers-Cowboys on Prime Video, which generated an audience of 16.725 million for the Week 5 Thursday night game. This week, it's Cowboys-Packers on Sunday night. And the numbers will surely reflect the presence of two significant teams with multiple star players, in a game that will have a significant impact on the standings in the NFC, given that the Cowboys are 2-3 and the Packers are 3-2.

stories.title: The Colts are hoping to get Jonathan Taylor back on track when they host the winless Titans
stories.summary: The Indianapolis Colts need Jonathan Taylor to become a big-play threat again.
stories.detailText: The Indianapolis Colts need Jonathan Taylor to become a big-play threat again. He's gone 12 straight games without rushing for 100 yards. He's been held scoreless two of the last three weeks. And after he was held to a season-low 45 yards in last week's loss at Pittsburgh, the Colts will do everything they can to get him running right Sunday. “The NFL run game is an 11-man run game. Everybody on the field is important,” Colts offensive coordinator Jim Bob Cooter said. “Obviously, J.T. has been so valuable for us over the years, but we’re all pushing to improve our level of play, improve our level of coaching. It’s not all statistically based, but we’re looking to improve.” There may be no better chance to get Taylor rolling than this week, when the Colts (2-3) host winless Tennessee . Run defense hasn't been the Titans' problem. Tennessee is ranked near the middle of the pack, yielding 114 yards per game, and veterans such as All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and safety Amani Hooker know what to expect from having gone against Taylor twice a season since 2020. The biggest priority for first-year Titans coach Robert Saleh is getting production out of the offense and quarterback Cam Ward . How bad has it been? Saleh is routinely answering questions about whether Ward, last year's No. 1 draft pick, will continue to start. “Are there things he has to do better? Yes,” Saleh said this week. “Has he improved? Yes. I think we can agree that that was the case (Week 4) when we were up here having the same conversation. And was (Week 5) a step back? Yes, but it was a step back as an entire offense, not just Cam.” Ward has thrown just three touchdown passes this season and the same number of interceptions while completing just 63.2% of his throws. His woes have contributed to a nearly 11-minute disparity in time of possession for the Titans, and if that happens again Sunday, Taylor can expect to carry a heavy workload — and that could open the door for some game-changing runs. “He sees it right, he hits it right, we'll be good,” Colts coach Shane Steichen said. “Obviously, the chunk plays like we saw last year, we haven't had those in the run game, and it would be great to get back to that and get those explosives going forward.” Need to know Tennessee (0-5) vs. Indianapolis (2-3). When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, Fox. Latest odds: Colts by 7. Against the spread: Titans 2-3; Colts 3-2. Last week: Titans lost to the Texans 26-3; Colts lost to the Steelers 34-22. Last meeting: Colts beat the Titans 38-14 on Oct. 26, 2025, in Indianapolis. Series record: Colts lead 41-22. Matchup to watch Ward vs. Colts defense. The quarterback and new offensive coordinator Brian Daboll have at times not appeared to be on the same page. Could this be the week Ward turns it around? Perhaps. He's facing a defense coming off yet another abysmal performance. But Indy’s defense has been here before — at home against a winless AFC South team, looking to change direction. The Colts responded by beating Houston in Week 3 and remain hopeful of a repeat in Week 6. Stats and stuff — Indy has won six straight in the series. Tennessee won the previous five. — Tennessee's next victory would give Ward his fourth career win and Saleh his first with the franchise. It would also be the 500th all-time win for the Titans. — Simmons needs one sack to pass Ted Washington (45) to move into 10th on the franchise's career list and fourth during the Titans era (1999-present). — Tennessee LB Anthony Hill Jr . opened his rookie season by recording five or more tackles in all five games. — The Titans' top three rushers ( Tony Pollard , Tyjae Spears and Ward) have 99 total carries this season, two fewer than the Colts' Taylor. — With 4 yards rushing, Taylor will become the fifth player since 2000 to reach 8,000 yards in 90 or fewer games. stories.title: Chargers' Mike McDaniel 'always' coaching for his job: 'Insulting to do anything else'
stories.summary: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel says he approaches every game as if he were coaching for his job, but he knows the pressure is on amid an 0-5 start.
stories.detailText: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel stands on the field before a loss to the Las Vegas Raiders at SoFi Stadium on Sept. 20. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel didn’t shy away from discussing his job security Thursday amid a frustrating 0-5 start to the season. “I feel like it’s core to my job to always feel that way,” McDaniel said when asked if he’s coaching for his job. “I need to do the very best I possibly can, all the time, because [of] the players, the organization, the fans. “So, that’s second nature. … I think it’s disrespectful to all those that choose to invest in our game and our team to not look at things that way. The second you get comfortable in this league, it’s a wrap; it’s too good. I will be doing my very best, because from an integrity standpoint, I think it’s really insulting to do anything else. And that won’t change.” Read more: NFL Week 6 picks: Panthers defeat Eagles; Packers beat Cowboys McDaniel says his determination is unwavering. His place in the Chargers’ organization, however, might not be if things don’t change soon. The Chargers, who rank 10th in total yards allowed per game on defense (311.6), enter Sunday’s road game against the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs averaging just 16.8 points per game, the third-lowest mark in the NFL above just the also-winless Miami Dolphins (14.0) and Tennessee Titans (11.6). Quarterback Justin Herbert ranks 22nd in passing (937 passing yards) and is last in the NFL in total quarterback rating (26.6). Injuries have played a significant role in the Chargers’ offensive struggles. Eight offensive players either didn’t practice or were limited in practice because of injuries on Wednesday. Four rookies started on the offensive line in Sunday’s loss to the Denver Broncos and wide receivers Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Brenen Thompson, didn’t play. McDaniel insists that he’s been giving the franchise all he has. “I would be so embarrassed if I told you, ‘Well, now I’m going to try harder,’” McDaniel said. “Like, what? What have you been doing? I’m confident in the players that we have. The improvement that I see before the results generally lead to good things. But talk is cheap. We got to do.” Get the best, most interesting and strangest stories of the day from the L.A. sports scene and beyond from our newsletter The Sports Report. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

stories.title: Jayden Daniels on clock debacle: "Ultimately, it's on me"
stories.summary: When it comes to the Week 5 overtime clock debacle for the Commanders, both coach Dan Quinn and quarterback Jayden Daniels continue to take the blame for the failure to stop the clock before a potential game-winning field.
stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pft_danielsquinn_261014","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"","duration":"637270","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pft_danielsquinn_261014","genre":"News, Trending","guid":"nbc_pft_danielsquinn_261014","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"ProFootballTalk","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"Green Bay Packers, Washington Commanders","title": "Quinn, Daniels have questions to answer","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/dan-quinn-jayden-daniels-have-questions-to-answer-after-all-time-mistake","availableDate":"2026-10-14T12:55:04Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} When it comes to the Week 5 overtime clock debacle for the Commanders, both coach Dan Quinn and quarterback Jayden Daniels continue to take the blame for the failure to stop the clock before a potential game-winning field. In his midweek press conference, Daniels again accepted responsibility for the outcome. " Ultimately, like, it’s on me ," Daniels told reporters. "At the end of the day, I know [coach Dan Quinn] is getting a lot of slack for it, whatever, you know, but regardless of what happens, I'm the person on the field that's supposed to calm everything, control everything, and I failed to the standard I hold myself to and the standard in this organization. So it's just something for me to move on. I'm not saying I'm proud of it or anything. Obviously, looking back, like, it could have resulted in a loss, we tied, but it was a fail in my in my eyes and, you know, I know I'm better in that. I hold myself to a higher standard than that. So, moving forward, I'll grow from and learn from it. And it'll never happen again." He also was asked for his reaction to the external criticism. "I'm moving on to San Francisco," Daniels said. "I can't say it's not warranted because of what happened. You know, everybody has opinions to say, opinions to speak, and rightfully so, so I can't stop nobody for saying their opinion or anything like that. It's just about my process and moving forward and learning from it, moving on." It's still unclear how it happened, and Daniels has not been asked whether he thought that overtime would continue for a second period. While that would be a very plausible explanation for the failure to get the clock stopped before time ran out, it would open another can of worms. Regardless, it all goes back to the coaching staff — to offensive coordinator David Blough and to head coach Dan Quinn. Blough has yet to face reporters regarding his role in the situation. Regardless, Quinn hired Blough (after firing Kliff Kingsbury), and Quinn entrusted Blough with the offense. Beyond that, it's Quinn's third year with Daniels. Sunday's glitch was a symptom of a potentially deeper issue, when it comes to attention to detail and/or willingness and ability to take charge in a moment of chaos. Quinn either failed to spot it, or he failed to fix it.

stories.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. set to debut for Texans in London against Jaguars, Parker Washington
stories.summary: — Plenty of attention will be on Marvin Harrison Jr. when the receiver makes his Houston Texans debut on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.
stories.detailText: LONDON -- — Plenty of attention will be on Marvin Harrison Jr . when the receiver makes his Houston Texans debut on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. There’s an unheralded Jacksonville receiver, though, whose been making big plays at key times: Parker Washington . And especially in London. Washington caught two touchdown passes from Trevor Lawrence last Sunday in an improbable 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. His leaping, twisting grab in the end zone had given the Jags a fourth-quarter lead. "He’s a huge playmaker for us,” Lawrence said. “You’ve seen all the different things he can do. He’s great after the catch, he’s physical through contact. He’s made some unbelievable contested catches. He’s good over the middle. “So, you look at a guy that can do all that, and it opens up a lot for your offense.” The 5-foot-10 Washington, drafted in 2023 by the Jags in the sixth round pick out of Penn State, leads the team with 22 receptions for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He also contributes on special teams. Washington returned a punt 96 yards for a touchdown in 2024 against the Patriots at Wembley Stadium, where the Jaguars will “host” the Texans to complete their London doubleheader. Sunday’s AFC South matchup brings to mind last season’s game in which Houston overcame a 19-point deficit in the fourth quarter to beat the Jags 36-29 with backup quarterback Davis Mills at the helm while CJ Stroud was out injured. “Obviously, have a tough feeling in our stomachs from the last time we played against these guys,” Jags coach Liam Coen said. ”(We) know that every time that you line up against this team, it’s going to be a fight, it’s going to be a brawl. That’s what’s great about football, that’s what’s great about rivalries.” After losing in Houston last season, Jacksonville closed out its regular season with eight straight wins. The Texans were set to arrive in London on Friday morning. They earned their first win of the season last week by beating the Titans 26-3 . “Defensively, the thing that went well for us is we got off the field on third down,” coach DeMeco Ryans said. “We took the football away and we stopped the run. We didn’t give up many explosive passes. That was something that was hurting us the first couple weeks.” Ryans had taken over defensive play-calling duties ahead of the Tennessee game. Need to know Houston (1-4) vs. Jacksonville (4-1) at Wembley Stadium. When/where to watch: Sunday, 9:30 a.m., EDT, NFL Network. Latest odds: Jaguars by 2 1/2 Against the spread: Houston 1-4, Jacksonville 3-2. Last week: Texans beat Titans 26-3; Jaguars beat Eagles 19-17. Last meeting: Texans beat Jaguars 36-29 on Nov. 9, 2025, in Houston. Series record: Texans lead 32-16. Matchup to watch The Jaguars offensive line against Houston’s pass rush. The Jaguars lost starting left tackle Anton Harrison against the Eagles. He will have knee surgery when the team returns home from London. Veteran lineman Walker Little will take his place. Through Week 5, the Texans had the second-most sacks — 18 — in the NFL. Defensive end Will Anderson Jr . leads the NFL with 7 1/2 sacks — including three last week — and 10 tackles for loss this season. Danielle Hunter has three sacks. Lawrence fumbled twice on strip-sacks last week; both were recovered by the Jags. Stats and stuff — Trevor Lawrence has thrown at least one touchdown pass in each of his eight London starts for the Jags. That's the most international starts by a quarterback. His record in London is 5-3. — Jacksonville committed 13 penalties for 100 yards last week. — Houston quarterback C.J. Stroud has yet to throw an interception this season. — Marvin Harrison Jr.'s arrival gives the Texans another big receiver. The 6-foot-3, 220-pound Harrison can play opposite star Nico Collins , who is 6-4 and 222 pounds. — The Texans are tied for the most completions of 20-plus yards in the NFL this season. They have 21, along with the Rams and Bills entering Week 6. — Houston has had at least one sack in 26 straight games. The Texans had four sacks last week against Tennessee, extending their franchise record for most consecutive games with at least one sack. — The Jags won back-to-back London games in 2023 — beating the Atlanta Falcons at Wembley and then the Buffalo Bills at Tottenham. — Jacksonville leads the NFL in rushing defense (63.8 yards per game allowed) and by limiting the Eagles to 22 yards rushing last week became the second team in the Super Bowl era to not allow an opposing player to rush for 40 or more yards in their first five games of a season, joining the 1969 Dallas Cowboys . ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

stories.summary: Ogbo Okoronkwo was promoted to the 49ers active roster. Eugene Asante was added to the practice squad
stories.detailText: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers promoted Ogbo Okoronkwo to the active roster and signed linebacker Eugene Asante to the practice squad. Asante will likely be elevated for Monday Night Football with Dre Greenlaw suspended and Garret Wallow dealing with a hamstring injury. Asante ran a 4.48 40-yard dash and had a 10-yard split in the 96th percentile. He’s on the roster to cover kicks. Asante was an undrafted free agent out of Auburn in 2025. Asante spent time on the practice squads of the Dolphins, Browns, Falcons, and Cardinals. Raheem Morris should be able to vouch for the type of player Asante is. Arizona released him from its practice squad on October 13. The big news is the 49ers opening the practice window for wide receiver Christian Kirk. He’s been dealing with a calf injury since the first day of training camp. It’s been three and a half months since Kirk played football. The 49ers have two games before their bye. It’s reasonable to think the Niners will give Kirk a few weeks to get back up to speed and in football shape; that way, he can hit the ground running when they return from the bye. Kyle Shanahan said Kirk has had setbacks since he hurt his hamstring on the first day of training camp, which is why we haven’t seen him in so long. Shanahan said Kirk had a “real good week and an awesome weekend,” so Thursday’ll be Kirk’s first official day back. Here are the injuries for Thursday’s practice: Out: WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring) LB Garret Wallow (hamstring) DT James Thompson (ankle) EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) S Marques Sigle (ankle WR Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) Limited: DB Siran Neal (neck) RT Colton McKivitz (sick) FB Kyle Juszczyk (knee) WR Christian Kirk (calf) CB Upton Stout (shoulder) Shanahan said Evans is dealing with Achilles soreness. As for Bosa’s availability for Monday night, Shanahan said, “Hoping he can go, but not going to practice today.” He believes it won’t be an injury that lingers for the rest of the season. Linebacker Nick Martin won’t return this week. There was speculation about Martin returning with Greenlaw and Wallow out, but Shanahan said, “He’s not getting up this week.” Deebo Samuel could head to the injured reserve. Shanahan said, “I think if we didn’t have that bye week, it’d be around that area. But gaining that week where we don’t play is still why we’re trying to wait on that right now. And hope we don’t have to do it.” Wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling is “a ways away,” but Shanahan thinks he’s on track. There’s an “outside chance” Demarcus Robinson returns before the bye week. Shanahan said they’re hoping to have him back after the bye, which is his way of saying that’s the expectation.

stories.title: Eric Bieniemy on Chiefs’ passionate moments: ‘It’s all about survival’
stories.summary: Kansas City’s offensive coordiantor explains his coaching style and relationship with players.
stories.detailText: (Photo by William Purnell/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images During the Kansas City Chiefs ’ Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders , the CBS broadcast showed quarterback Patrick Mahomes passionately conversating with a stoic Eric Bieniemy, the Chiefs’ offensive coordinator. Patrick Mahomes having a passionate rant towards Eric Bieniemy. 🎥 @sluggahjells pic.twitter.com/yJPg2xKs9B — The Whole Delivery (@TWDTV1) October 4, 2026 Sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson asked Reid about that moment at halftime, and he described it as “frustration and competitiveness ,“ according to Wolfson. On Thursday, ESPN’s Nate Taylor asked about the conversation during Bieniemy’s time at the podium. His answer offered insight into the coach-player relationship in Kansas City, between Bieniemy and Mahomes, or whoever else on the Chiefs’ offense. “I’m the one doing all the complaining for the most part,” Bieniemy said with a smile. “But I have no problems with guys venting their frustrations because I want them to; that’s part of the dynamics of the relationships that we have. “Sometimes, you’re going to agree with things, and sometimes you’re going to disagree with things, but if there’s something that has taken place out on the field, they may have a better point of view than what we do off the field, so I want them to feel comfortable coming to share that stuff with me,” Bieniemy said. The short video made it clear that Bieniemy was listening to Mahomes and making an effort to hear him out. It’s part of his coaching style and his overall mentality as a former player. “There is no issue of communication,” Bieniemy clarified. “We play in the arena; it’s all about survival… You’re inviting all of that because I’d rather him come and vent his frustrations at me than to vent it in a different place where it’s not going to be taken the right way.” The discussion occurred during the first half, before the team put up 20 points in the fourth quarter and put away a motivated Raiders team. Conversations like that can make the difference between a win and a loss. The Chiefs didn’t make it easy on themselves in Las Vegas or in the Week 3 win over the Miami Dolphins . The biggest factor toward that on offense has been the lack of short-yardage success. Bieniemy alluded to that when describing Kansas City’s offense so far this season. “We’re still working on establishing our foundation; we’re still working on establishing who we are as an offense,” Bieniemy shared. “I know that we’ve done some good things, but there have been some things that we’ve done extremely shitty that we need to improve upon.” The Chiefs rank ninth in third-down conversion rate and 12th on fourth downs , but the few failures have come at inopportune times. In Week 1, running back Kenneth Walker found a 60-yard touchdown run on fourth and short; in the last two weeks, the backfield hasn’t navigated the trenches as well. “One thing I always tell the backs is this: regardless [of whether] we block anyone, it’s our duty and our responsibility to find a way to move the ball, to find a way to move the chains,” Bieniemy said. “There are offensive linemen, tight ends, everyone is involved,” Bieniemy elaborated. “Right now, we’re just doing okay in short yardage. We have to be better collectively as a group.” Moving forward, the team should have left guard Kingsley Suamataia helping make room for the backs and possibly left tackle Josh Simmons as well. He is back on the practice field this week. Rookie left tackle Kahlil Benson has done an admirable job filling in; if he moves to the bench at some point, don’t be surprised if he’s still used to move the chains on third and fourth downs.

A Cardinals second-round pick in 2018, Kirk has registered 432 receptions for 5,415 yards with 30 touchdowns in his career. Jeanty, who has not been 100% healthy since sustaining an ankle sprain in late August, had his worst rushing performance of the season in the 45-17 road loss, totaling 27 yards on 10 carries. "Unless I can't run, jump or cut, I'm playing," Jeanty said after the loss to New England. "Football is a tough game. You're never gonna play feeling 100%. At the end of the day, I want to go out there and do my best for my teammates."

teamStories.summary: Klint Kubiak talked about making changes up front, and that will be tested on Sunday
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 6 is an opportunity for the Las Vegas Raiders to bounce back after back-to-back losses, including last week’s blowout in New England . However, that certainly won’t come easy against the 4-1 Buffalo Bills , who currently have the best Super Bowl odds (+750) of any AFC team, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . In other words, if the Raiders are going to prove to be a legitimate playoff contender in 2026, they need to win the key matchups below. Raiders’ OL vs. Rousseau, Walker Part of the reason for Las Vegas’ two-game skid is that quarterback Kirk Cousins has been under pressure more frequently. According to Pro Football Focus , Cousins was pressured on 33 of his 101 dropbacks ( 32.7% ) in Weeks 1 through 3, and he’s faced pressure on 34 of 83 dropbacks ( 41.0% ) in the last two games combined. Two of the biggest culprits on the Raiders’ offensive line are left guard Spencer Burford and left tackle Kolton Miller. Granted, Burford only gave up one pressure against the Chiefs, but he surrendered five and posted a 0.0 pass-blocking grade against the Patriots. Also, the five-year veteran has yielded the most pressures ( 18 ) of any guard in the NFL for the season so far, meaning pass protection has been an issue for him beyond the last two games. That’s forced the left tackle to give his guard more help, contributing to a slip in Miller’s production. He was beaten for just five pressures in Weeks 1 through 3 combined before losing 12 times in the last two weeks . To be fair, not all of Miller’s issues are tied to Burford. The former has plenty of room for individual improvement, too, specifically with how he handles power rushers. Meanwhile, the Bills’ defense has an up-and-coming pass-rush duo with edge-rusher Greg Rousseau and defensive tackle Deone Walker. Rousseau has posted six sacks in five games, which is two shy of tying a career high, and leads his position with 35 pressures, per PFF . Now, the 26-year-old has primarily lined up as a left outside linebacker or on the right side of the offensive line so far this season. However, he’s had more snaps on the right side every game since Week 2, topping out at 19 snaps against the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football . Given Miller’s struggles and the fact Rousseau primarily wins with power, the left tackle’s weakness, expect Buffalo to at least test Vegas’ blindside protector with its best pass-rusher on Sunday. On the interior, Walker has spent almost as much time as a right defensive tackle ( 89 snaps ) as he has on the left side (93) this season. So, he’ll likely be testing Burford, or whoever is in at left guard for the Silver and Black. On paper, that’s a favorable matchup for Buffalo since the 2025 fourth-round pick heads into the game ranking third among defensive tackles with 21 pressures . Granted, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak hinted at some offensive line changes during his press conference on Monday. That could mean Burford will be on the bench this Sunday. But regardless of who is in the trenches, the offensive line has to have an answer for Rousseau and Walker. The Bills defense has been bad this season, tying for the most points per game allowed ( 32.8 ) and giving up the fourth-most yards per game (396.2). So, if the Silver and Black can keep those two defensive linemen in check, their offense should be able to move the ball and put points on the board. Leonard vs. Brady Sure, play-callers could be a “key matchup” every game, but this one feels more or extra important for Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard. Leonard started hot, keeping the Miami Dolphins and Los Angeles Chargers to 13 and 14 points, respectively, in his first two games ever as a coordinator. However, the book is out on his tendacies and Vegas is averaging 34.0 points per game allowed over the last three weeks. The Silver and Black are feeling the effects of having a first-time defensive play-caller. It wasn’t as prevalent against the New Orleans Saints, but the Kansas City Chiefs and New England Patriots seemingly had the answers to the test with perfect play calls for what the Raiders were running, especially on money downs. Now, an offensive coordinator turned head coach, Joe Brady, comes into town. During his three seasons as Buffalo’s offensive coordinator, Brady’s offenses ranked fourth, 10th and fourth in yards , and sixth, second and fourth in points. After getting promoted to head coach in the offseason while retaining offensive play-calling duties, he hasn’t skipped a beat with the No. 4 offense in terms of yards and No. 1 in points so far in 2026. Those aren’t exactly encouraging numbers for a struggling first-time defensive coordinator, but Leonard has to start making adjustments. The foundation of his scheme is solid (it’s very similar to Mike Macdonald’s with the Seattle Seahawks), showcasing a lot of creativity. But it might be time to reverse course and simplify the play calls because he’s losing the element of surprise. For example, Sumer Sports has the Raiders rotating safeties 44.0% of the time, the second-highest rate in the NFL. Changing up the pre- and post-snap looks works when the opposing quarterback isn’t expecting it or is caught off-guard. But when it’s that frequent, they can just expect the picture to change and take advantage of defenders being out of position since the defenders have to sprint to their spots rather than lining up in them. It’s all part of the chess match, which Leonard is still learning at this stage in his career. But if Las Vegas is going to pull off an upset on Sunday, he needs to be a quick study. Stukes vs. Allen Josh Allen was the NFL MVP two years ago and has looked like one of the early favorites to win the award for a second time in 2026. To put it in perspective, he’s averaging 30 more passing yards ( 219.5 to 249.8 ) and 16 more rushing yards (31.2 to 47.8) per game than he did in 2024. Also, he leads the league with eight rushing touchdowns and has seven scores through the air so far this season. Allen is one of those quarterbacks where if a defense tries to take away everything, they’ll end up taking away nothing. He’s become so dynamic that the strategy shifts to just trying to limit the damage and then forcing him into a mistake or two. One way to do that is to get the MVP candidate to play hero ball and force passes downfield. The Wyoming product has always been known for his arm strength and gunslinger mentality. This season, he’s tied for sixth with 23 pass attempts of 20 or more yards past the line of scrimmage, per PFF , but isn’t having much success. Allen has only completed nine of those attempts for a 39.1 completion percentage that is tied for 22nd among qualifying quarterbacks (minimum five deep passes). Also, six of his seven “turnover-worthy plays” have come on deep shots for the highest TWP rate (22.2%) on said throws in the league. Meanwhile, another aspect of the Raiders’ defensive regression is that they’ve only turned the ball over once in the last two games — a forced fumble against the Patriots — and haven’t had an interception since Week 3. Given Allen’s propensity to push the ball downfield, the spotlight will be on Vegas’ free safety, Treydan Stukes. Stukes only has one pick so far, stepping in front of a deep pass from Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis in the season opener. Also, the rookie is coming off the worst game of his young career, making a few coverage mistakes in New England. However, the Arizona product was known for his ball skills in college, recording seven career interceptions , including four last year. Additionally, he’s been a solid first-year defender in the three other games he’s played during the campaign. That being said, the Raiders need Stukes to be on his “A-game” and take advantage if/when Allen gives him an opportunity to create a momentum-shifting play.
